newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - modest gains on day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - modest gains on day.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices managed only modest gains Thursday despite the 30-year U.S. Treasury benchmark's 1-1/8 point gain.
"I'd say we are up 1/4 of a point," a trader said. "We're not running with the Treasury market at all."

Though bid lists circulated Thursday, munis are really suffering from a lack of cash, the trader said. While players tend to look forward to January re-investment cash, much of that cash came in last month, he said.
"Most of that re-investment stuff is taken care of in December, particularly for the real size money, the institutions, and the mutual funds, and the insurance companies," the trader said.
Retail investors tend to postpone buying until the money hits their accounts, he said, adding that the market has benefitted from some retail interest.
"But there is not a big splash of cash going to work," the trader said.

December buyers were probably wise because though munis have cheapened since then, that month's relatively substantial menu of new issues offered a better selection for buyers. With few new issues of late, buyers have a hard time finding size and structure, he said.

"If you waited, you'd be looking at secondary offerings," the trader said. "It's not just a level today, it's more 'I need X structure...' I think in the long run, that's what most people are holding out for, the right structure."
A municipal analyst said the overall muni cash market was up 1/4 point plus.
Dollar bonds largely mirrored the broader market's rise, while high-grade issues improved by two basis points overall and by three basis points on the long end, he said.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract closed up 16/32 at 115-3/32. The March T-bond contract closed up 22/32 at 111-13/32. The MOB spread was 118 ticks.
In the goverment cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed up 1-4/32 at 96-25/32 to yield 6.75 percent. Treasuries got an early lift from the December producer prices data.

Overall PPI was up 0.5 percent, but because the gain was largely attributable to higher energy prices, the market looked past it to the scant 0.1 percent rise in the core rate. The core rate excludes the more volatile food and energy prices.
December employment figures are due on Friday, and economists polled by Reuters expect non-farm payrolls to grow by 192,000 versus 118,000 in the previous report.
"I think that's a number that is going to be widely watched," a municipal trader said, adding that he heard estimates for a 200,000 rise in payrolls.
"I think anything at or around that level will probably be perceived as positive," he said. "Anything above it (will) put us back on (Federal Reserve) alert right off the bat."

Next week's negotiated deals are expected to number 31 and total nearly $2 billion. Topping the list is a $550 million of tax-exempt New York City general obligation bonds Wednesday via Goldman Sachs & Co. On Tuesday, Dade County, Fla., is expected to sell $423 million bonds through PaineWebber Inc.
Sixty two competitive deals are expected next week totaling $997 million, the largest being a $195 million North Carolina deal Wednesday at 1100 EST.
